validity.researcher_notes: Existence/classification/duplicate all check out. This is a genuine, distinct FERC facility -- the FERC EA's own facilities table (Table A-2) lists 'Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border' as a separate line item (MP 0.0-0.3, McKenzie County, subtotal 0.3 mi) from 'Tioga-Elkhorn Creek' (62.8 mi), 'Line Section 25 Loop' (20.3 mi), 'Line Section 30 Loop' (9.6 mi) and 'Tioga Compressor Lateral' (0.5 mi) -- so P3588 is NOT a duplicate of P3584/P3585/P3586/P3587; all five are five physically distinct pipe segments of one FERC-authorized project (Docket CP20-52), each correctly a separate GEM row. Prose confirms the exact facts on the sheet: 'The Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border pipeline would include about 0.3 mile of new 24-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline between the proposed Elkhorn Creek Compressor Station and the new interconnect with Northern Border in McKenzie County. The pipeline would have an MAOP of 1,480 psig.' (FERC EA p.10). Length=0.30 mi and Diameter=24.00 in both confirmed verbatim, naming this exact segment -- not an aggregate/system figure. CAVEAT on Capacity: the sheet's Capacity=250 MMcf/d is the project's overall incremental design capacity (FERC EA: 'incremental firm transportation design capacity of 250,000 [sic -- FERC's own text repeats this typo three times; the physically sensible reading, confirmed by WBI Energy's own project page and by Minot Daily News quoting Sen. Hoeven, is 250 MMcf/d, not 250,000] MMcf/d'; WBI Energy: 'Providing up to 250 million cubic feet per day'). That figure is identical across all five North Bakken Expansion segment rows in the roster (P3584-P3588), which is the classic aggregate-on-a-segment pattern the batch brief flags -- BUT for THIS specific row it is plausibly correct rather than an error: Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border shares the trunk's MAOP (1,480 psig, same as Tioga-Elkhorn Creek and Tioga Compressor Lateral) and is the sole final segment carrying gas to the Northern Border interconnect, i.e. it is on the main through-path that must carry the full incremental volume, unlike the two loop segments (Line Section 25 Loop MAOP 1,098 psig, Line Section 30 Loop MAOP 700 psig) which sit on a different pressure/flow regime and are a better candidate for the aggregate-figure concern -- see cross_row_leads for P3585/P3586. Not flagging a spec concern on P3588 itself. Owner/Operator = WBI Energy Transmission, Inc. 100% is correct and independently confirmed (FERC docket applicant of record + WBI Energy's own site, 'An MDU Resources Group Company' -- no dissolved/rolled-up entity here, unlike several other rows in this batch). Location (North Dakota start and end, McKenzie/Williams/Mountrail/Burke Counties) confirmed. Status=operating confirmed live: WBI's own project page (dateModified 2023-01-25) describes it in the present/completed tense with no idle/abandonment language, consistent with FERC's authorization and the Feb 2022 in-service date. Opened 5 of this row's 8 harvested wiki citations (FERC EA PDF, WBI Energy project page, Minot Daily News); the WBI 'north-bakken-handout.pdf' and Williston Herald links are dead (404) and nsenergybusiness.com blocked the fetch (403 Varnish); web.archive.org's availability API 429'd on every retry this session (rate limit, not a ban) so I did not obtain Wayback substitutes for those three -- not chased further given three solid independent primaries already corroborate every fact. The 8th citation (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php) is a generic data-portal root, not an article naming this pipeline, so it was not usable as a ref regardless.

cross_row_leads.facts: Tioga-Elkhorn Creek pipeline: 62.8 mi, 24-inch diameter, MAOP 1,480 psig, Williams/McKenzie Counties ND, MP 0.0-62.8, bi-directional flow. Matches GEM exactly. NOTE: Minot Daily News (2021-07, same URL used on P3588) instead describes 'about 60 miles of new 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline' for the trunk -- conflicts with both FERC's EA and WBI Energy's own 'Key Stats' ('62.8 miles of 24-inch diameter natural gas pipeline'). Two sources (FERC + WBI) agree on 24-inch; the newspaper's '20-inch' looks like a reporter error (likely conflated with the Tioga Compressor Lateral, which genuinely is 20-inch) -- flag but do not action without independent review.

Line Section 25 Loop: 20.3 mi, 12-inch diameter, MAOP 1,098 psig (looping an existing 8-inch line, MAOP raised from 700 to 1,098 psig), Williams/Mountrail/Burke Counties, bi-directional. Matches GEM's len=20.3/dia=12.00. Also: in conjunction with this loop, WBI removed ~0.1 mi of an existing 6-inch Stoneview-Conoco lateral and built ~665 ft of new 8-inch mainline to the Norse Transfer Station -- a related but separate minor facility, not itself a GEM row as far as this sweep found. CAPACITY FLAG: this segment's MAOP (1,098 psig) differs materially from the main through-path (1,480 psig on Tioga-Elkhorn Creek, Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border and Tioga Compressor Lateral), which is a better candidate than P3588 for the 'aggregate 250 MMcf/d restated on every segment' concern the batch brief raised -- worth checking whether this loop's actual incremental capacity differs from the trunk's.

Line Section 30 Loop: 9.6 mi, 12-inch diameter, MAOP 700 psig, Williams County, between the existing Nesson Valve Setting and the Tioga Compressor Station, bi-directional. Matches GEM's len=9.6/dia=12.00. Same capacity-aggregation flag as P3585: MAOP 700 psig is well below the trunk's 1,480 psig, suggesting this loop's true incremental capacity contribution may differ from the uniform 250 MMcf/d on the sheet.

Tioga Compressor Lateral: 0.5 mi, 20-inch diameter, MAOP 1,480 psig, between the Tioga Plant Receipt Station and the new facilities at Tioga Compressor Station, Williams County. Matches GEM's len=0.5/dia=20.00 exactly. This is the segment the Minot Daily News '20-inch' description likely actually refers to (see P3584 lead).

ProposalYear=2020/ProposalMonth=2 (WBI Energy filed the FERC application Feb 14, 2020, Docket CP20-52) and ConstructionYear=2021/ConstructionMonth=7 (construction began July 2021 per Minot Daily News + WBI's own site) apply identically to all five North Bakken Expansion segment rows (P3584-P3588), not just P3588 -- same underlying project, one docket, one construction mobilization.

Sen. John Hoeven is quoted calling the North Bakken Expansion a '$260 million infrastructure project' -- a whole-project cost figure, not disaggregated by segment. Useful project-level context but not stageable as any one segment's SegmentCost (aggregate-vs-segment rule).
